# A long odd integer product removes every global heavy fiber but preserves the all-menu obstruction

Status: independent full audit PASS in \`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)\`.

This note strengthens the scope of
\`candidate e52160c774656005\`.
The same strict individual-capacity obstruction persists in a body with NO fiber of mass at least \(2^{-n}\) of the total. The example still has only one deepest source, leaving substantial parity slack; it is not a below-OC example.

The new dependency is the already proved all-normal paired-tail theorem and its strict \(d\geq3\) equality refinement:
\`candidate 732b11a769399016\`,
\`candidate d494e7e71949ac0b\`.
In dimension four, for a uniform simplex point X with centroid g,
\[
\Pr(u\cdot(X-g)\geq s)+\Pr(u\cdot(X-g)\geq-s)
\geq2\Gamma_4,
\]
strictly when \(s\ne0\). At zero shift equality requires a canonical vertex direction. The proofs and localization hypotheses are in those dependencies.

## 1. Actual product and its measure

Use the thin-edge body \(C_\delta\) from the companion source, with old integer coordinate z, fibers \(T,D_\delta,D_\delta\), endpoint volume \(v=\alpha V\), and unique smoothed deepest point \(Y_{\delta,h}=(0,y_{\delta,h})\). Let its raw maximal depth be \(Q_{\delta,h}\), its total mass \(M_0=V+2v\), and its actual within-fiber covariance norm be \(\Gamma_\delta\).

Introduce a SECOND integer coordinate t and take
\[
\widehat C_\delta=C_\delta\times[-2,2]
\]
with coordinate order \((z,t,x)\). Its fifteen sampled fibers are
\[
\widehat K_{z,t}=K_z,\qquad z=-1,0,1,\quad t=-2,-1,0,1,2.
\]
Every fiber is positive four-dimensional. Total mass is
\[
\widehat M=5(V+2v)>5V.
\]
Each fiber has volume at most V, so
\[
\max_{z,t}|\widehat K_{z,t}|<\widehat M/4.
\]
Thus the n=2 heavy-fiber proof does not apply. Repeating all old fibers five times leaves the pooled within-fiber covariance EXACTLY unchanged, so the actual smoothing norm and width are the same as in the old problem.

## 2. The actual deepest base must be (0,0)

At \((0,0,g)\), the five middle T fibers alone have every ordinary cap mass at least \(5\Gamma_4V\), by pairing t with -t and using the paired-tail theorem. Outward smoothing only increases capture. Pure-base halfspaces through this point contain at least three entire middle fibers. Hence
\[
\widehat Q_{\delta,h}\geq5\Gamma_4V. \tag{1}
\]

Any point with old base \(z=\pm1\) has depth at most \(5v\): a sufficiently large finite old base tilt isolates that endpoint column, and its total mass is \(5v\). This is smaller than (1).

At base \((0,t)\) with \(t=\pm1,\pm2\), use a large new-base tilt toward the closer end of the t interval. It captures at most one full old copy of mass \(M_0\); the copy at its own t level can independently use an arbitrary old cap via a fixed finite old-base tilt. Thus its depth is at most
\[
M_0+Q_{\delta,h}
\leq(1+\Gamma_4+3\alpha)V+C h.
\]
For sufficiently small \(\delta,h\), this is less than \(5\Gamma_4V\), since \(1+\Gamma_4<5\Gamma_4\). For \(t=\pm2\) the bound improves by omitting \(M_0\).

Consequently every deepest base is \((0,0)\). Restricting to caps with new tilt b=0 gives at a point y on that fiber
\[
\widehat{\operatorname{depth}}(0,0,y)
\leq5\,\operatorname{depth}_{C_\delta}(0,y).
\]
Together with (1) and the own-depth upper estimate in the companion note, every deepest y is in a uniform core and tends to g as \(\delta,h\downarrow0\). In particular active nonvertical caps are attained and have positive own coarea.

## 3. Uniform localization of every potentially minimizing new cap

Write a normalized nonvertical cap through \((0,0,y)\) as
\[
a z+b t+u\cdot(x-y)\geq0,\qquad \Gamma_\delta(u)=1.
\]
We claim that every cap of mass at most \(5Q_{\delta,h}\), for any mark y tending to g as above, has b arbitrarily small and u in arbitrarily small canonical vertex cones, when \(\delta,h\) are sufficiently small.

Only the five middle T contributions are needed to prove this. If \(|b|\) exceeds a uniform bound, the two middle layers on one side are full and the opposite two are empty; their total middle mass is
\[
2V+\text{the own T mass}\geq(2+\Gamma_4-o(1))V,
\]
which exceeds \(5Q_{\delta,h}=(5\Gamma_4+o(1))V\), since \(2-4\Gamma_4>0\). Thus b is uniformly bounded.

Suppose the claim failed along \(\delta_l,h_l\downarrow0\). Normalize u by the uniformly nondegenerate covariance norm and take a subsequence with \(u_l\to u,\ b_l\to b,\ y_l\to g\). The five middle masses converge to the ordinary five-layer cap mass; each cutting plane has ordinary T-volume zero. By the paired-tail theorem it is at least \(5\Gamma_4V\). If b is nonzero, at least the pair t=±1 is STRICTLY above \(2\Gamma_4V\), so the sum is strictly above the permitted limit. Hence b=0. At b=0, equality of all five identical contributions forces u to be one of the canonical simplex minimizing normals. This contradiction proves the claim.

Pure-base caps are also excluded at these low levels: through \((0,0)\), they contain all five middle fibers if b=0 and at least three if b is nonzero. Both exceed \(5Q_{\delta,h}\) for small parameters.

This is an all-normal compactness argument. It does not assume that adding symmetric integer noise preserves the active family without checking equality.

## 4. The new tilt is EXACTLY zero for every active cap

Use the small canonical cones and small b range supplied by Section3. Every middle T cut, including its entire smoothing strip and the shifts at t=-2,...,2, strictly isolates the same simplex vertex. For fixed u, its ordinary cap mass as a function of threshold is a positive constant times the fourth power of a positive affine function. Uniform outward smoothing averages such fourth powers over the common width interval. Thus its smoothed tail \(F_u(s)\) has strictly positive second derivative throughout this range.

The middle contribution at new tilt b is
\[
\sum_{t=-2}^2 F_u(b t).
\]
Strict convexity and symmetry give
\[
\sum_{t=-2}^2 F_u(b t)\geq5F_u(0),
\]
with equality ONLY when b=0.

For the endpoint contribution the companion exact dichotomy survives unchanged:
* In a cone outside J, the endpoint contribution is nonnegative, and at b=0, a=0 it is exactly zero.
* In a J-cone, pair \((-1,t,x)\) with \((1,-t,R_Jx)\). Both integer tilt terms cancel. The uniformly positive sum of continuous margins gives outside mass at least \(5v\) for EVERY a,b. At b=0 a finite saturating old-base tilt attains exactly \(5v\).

Consequently, at any mark in the stated core, every low cap with b nonzero has mass STRICTLY larger than the b=0 competitor with the same continuous direction and the minimizing old-base status. In particular every actually active cap at a deepest point has b=0.

For completeness this also identifies the deepest point itself. At the old unique deepest mark \(y_{\delta,h}\), every cap with mass at most \(5Q_{\delta,h}\) is in the just-analyzed regime, and hence has mass at least five times the corresponding old minimizing-through-mark mass, which is at least \(5Q_{\delta,h}\). Caps above that threshold are harmless. Therefore its new depth is exactly \(5Q_{\delta,h}\). The b=0 upper bound from Section2 implies that any new deepest mark is an old deepest mark. The old uniqueness gives the new unique source
\[
\widehat Y_{\delta,h}=(0,0,y_{\delta,h}),\qquad
\widehat Q_{\delta,h}=5Q_{\delta,h}. \tag{2}
\]

A new active cap has b=0 and is exactly an old active cap repeated five times. Conversely every old active cap with b=0 is new-active. Thus the ENTIRE active family, not only a selected menu, has been identified.

## 5. Every menu and every physical field inherit the strict capacity upper bound

The full coarea of a lifted active cap is five times its old coarea. Its continuous normal is unchanged. Hence its balanced response menus, including all possible choices of old base tilt and all probability mixtures, coincide with the old response menus. Its boundary profile is independent of t and equals the old profile \(W(z,x)\).

Let \(\Phi(n,z,t,x)\geq0\) be any globally finite continuous physical field convex in the full physical point for each normal. For a fixed integer t, its restriction
\[
\Phi_t(n,z,x)=\Phi(n,z,t,x)
\]
is an admissible old physical field. The audited old full-cone inequality therefore gives
\[
\int W\Phi_t\,d\sigma_{\rm old}
\leq(\Gamma_4-\zeta_\delta)
       \int\Phi_t\,d\sigma_{\rm old}
\]
for every t and EVERY actual menu. Summing over the five t values proves
\[
\int_{\partial\widehat S}W\Phi\,d\widehat\sigma
\leq(\Gamma_4-\zeta_\delta)
       \int_{\partial\widehat S}\Phi\,d\widehat\sigma. \tag{3}
\]
No full-ambient volume is substituted for mixed surface measure: the latter is exactly the finite sum of the four-dimensional fiber boundary measures.

Thus neither global absence of a heavy fiber nor permission to optimize over all active menus repairs the universal individual \(\Gamma_d\)-capacity statement.

## 6. What slack remains

The new integer dimension is two, and there is ONE actual deepest source, so only one of four possible source parities is occupied. The normalized maximal depth remains the same as in the original body, close to \(\Gamma_4\), whereas its OC target is \(\Gamma_4/4\). Therefore this example does not threaten a capacity-cost allocation paid by the full parity budget, nor a theorem restricted to actual below-OC body minima.

This is precisely the scope gained over the original heavy-middle example: a global heavy-fiber exclusion is insufficient, while source-count or geometric parity slack remains available.
